extracted.intended_audience: corporate managers, sustainability/reporting professionals, board members, and compliance teams preparing for CSRD reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for companies to prepare, produce and assure sustainability reporting that complies with the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). Covers who must comply, required disclosures, standards (ESRS), assurance, and preparatory steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must consider and report on two perspectives: (1) financial materiality — how sustainability issues impact the company's financial performance, position and development; and (2) environmental and social materiality — how the company's activities affect the environment and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must conduct a double materiality assessment to identify and prioritize sustainability matters material from both financial and impact perspectives. Example: report both how climate risks affect the business and how the business contributes to greenhouse gas emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must report in accordance with the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) developed by EFRAG to ensure consistency and comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESRS provide the framework and specific disclosure requirements covering climate, environment, social and governance matters. Reports should follow ESRS structure and metrics where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive ESG reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must provide detailed information across environmental, social and governance (ESG) matters, including climate change impacts, emissions reduction strategies, human rights practices, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures should be comprehensive and reliable so stakeholders (investors, customers, employees) have a clear picture of sustainability performance and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets, target metrics and transition plans (including net-zero alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must share sustainability targets, progress toward achieving them, and how those targets support a transition to a sustainable economy and achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 as required by EU laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative targets, timelines, indicators of progress, and narrative on how targets align with broader transition pathways (e.g., net-zero by 2050).

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and supply chain due diligence disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must disclose their due diligence process for identifying and mitigating social and environmental impacts in their value chains and supply chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe procedures, findings, remediation measures, and how supply-chain impacts were assessed. Stakeholders should be able to understand the full scope of the company's sustainability risks across its value chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party auditing and assurance (limited then reasonable assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainability information and data included in the report must be audited/assured by a third party; initially limited assurance is required, with a move to reasonable assurance within the next three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initially auditors provide limited assurance based mainly on the organisation's statements; within three years, assurance must be reasonable, relying on the auditor's examination and understanding of operations, processes and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of obligated entities (who needs to comply)
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRD applies to: large EU companies meeting at least two of: >250 employees, >€40 million net turnover, >€20 million total assets; all companies listed on EU-regulated markets (except listed micro-enterprises); non-EU companies with significant EU presence (EU turnover >€150 million or at least one EU subsidiary/branch); and listed SMEs (with simplified reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent companies are generally responsible for consolidated reporting; subsidiaries may be exempt if their sustainability information is included in the parent's consolidated report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated sustainability section in the management report
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must include a dedicated sustainability section in their management report covering a range of ESG topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section should be structured, comprehensive, and integrated with the rest of the management report to reflect sustainability risks, strategy and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate-related information aligned with the EU Taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must include climate-related disclosures that are aligned with the EU Taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose taxonomy-aligned activities, climate impacts, and how climate-related targets and activities map to taxonomy criteria where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental factors beyond climate (biodiversity, ecosystems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting must cover environmental issues beyond climate, such as biodiversity and ecosystems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe impacts, risks and mitigation measures related to biodiversity, ecosystems and other non-climate environmental factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and human rights matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must disclose social topics and human rights practices across operations and value chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information on policies, due diligence, identified impacts, remediation, and relevant metrics (e.g., labor practices, health & safety, human rights outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance practices and business ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting must cover governance arrangements and business ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose governance structures, oversight of sustainability issues, anti-corruption measures, and how ethics are embedded in strategy and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability risks and opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must report on sustainability-related risks and opportunities that affect their business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain identification, assessment and management of risks and opportunities, including scenario analysis where relevant (e.g., climate scenarios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of due diligence processes (internal processes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must describe their due diligence processes for identifying and addressing sustainability impacts and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain procedures, governance, stakeholder engagement, monitoring and remediation steps taken as part of the due diligence process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts along the value chain
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must disclose impacts (environmental and social) along the entire value chain, not only within the company's direct operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scope, methods and findings for upstream and downstream impact assessments, including supplier-related impacts and downstream product impacts where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards include sector-specific requirements acknowledging that different industries face unique sustainability challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the sector-tailored ESRS requirements where relevant; disclose how sector-specific impacts, risks and metrics are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary exemption for consolidated reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsidiaries may be exempt from separate reporting if their sustainability information is included in the parent company's consolidated report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consolidated reporting covers subsidiary impacts and disclosures comprehensively if claiming exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listed SME simplified reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) listed on EU-regulated markets are subject to simplified CSRD reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMEs should follow the tailored/simplified ESRS for listed SMEs; still plan for data collection and governance appropriate to size and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting quality: consistency, comparability and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRD aims to ensure sustainability information is consistent, comparable and reliable across companies and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement standardized metrics (ESRS), robust data systems, controls and assurance to achieve data quality and comparability for stakeholders and investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step — conduct a gap analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should identify differences between current reporting practices and CSRD/ESRS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the gap analysis to prioritise remediation, data collection needs, process changes and resource allocation to meet compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step — establish cross-functional teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Form cross-functional teams with members from various departments to coordinate sustainability reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include finance, legal, sustainability, operations, procurement, HR and IT to ensure comprehensive data collection and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step — invest in data systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement advanced systems for collecting and managing sustainability data to ensure accuracy and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise systems that support traceability, controls, automated collection, and integration with financial reporting systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step — engage with stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate with stakeholders (investors, customers, employees) to determine what sustainability information is most valuable and relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stakeholder input to shape materiality assessments, disclosures and prioritisation of issues for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step — develop a materiality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a process to assess and prioritise sustainability issues based on financial, environmental and social impacts (operationalise double materiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document methodology, stakeholder inputs, scoring/prioritisation criteria and how outcomes feed into disclosure decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step — train staff on reporting mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate employees about CSRD requirements and sustainability concepts so involved personnel understand roles and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted training for data owners, preparers, auditors and governance bodies on reporting processes and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation step — seek external expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Hire consultants or external experts to guide initial CSRD compliance, especially for first-time reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External advisors can help with gap analyses, ESRS interpretation, data system design, assurance readiness and materiality frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and interaction with other frameworks (SFDR and TCFD)
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRD is designed to work alongside and complement other initiatives: SFDR (financial sector disclosures) and TCFD (climate-related disclosures). CSRD is mandatory in the EU and incorporates many TCFD recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand overlaps and differences: SFDR focuses on financial market participants; TCFD is voluntary and climate-focused. Use alignment to streamline disclosures where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSRD objectives (transparency, accountability, investment decision utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The directive aims to increase transparency and accountability, facilitate better-informed investment decisions, drive corporate sustainability efforts, and support the transition to a sustainable economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reporting and governance to meet these objectives — e.g., make disclosures decision-useful for investors and stakeholders, and link reporting to strategy and risk management.
